pages.h: A phone maker that grew up
pages.t: Yealink was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Xiamen, China. It started with SIP phones and grew into a big name in business desk phones. The company is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
g: A desk phone that makes calls over the internet or a company network instead of an old phone line

pages.t: Today Yealink calls itself a leader in Unified Communications and Collaboration. The range covers IP phones, headsets, meeting room systems and cameras, plus management platforms for looking after all those devices.
g: Unified Communications: calls, meetings and messaging brought together on one platform

pages.h: Big claims, and whose they are
pages.t: Yealink says it is number 1 in global IP phone shipments and a top 5 video conferencing provider (it cites Frost and Sullivan, 2021). Those are Yealink's own claims on its website, so say "according to Yealink" when you repeat them to a reseller.

quiz.q: Which product areas does Yealink cover?
o: Phones, headsets, meeting room systems and management platforms
quiz.w: Yealink goes well beyond desk phones into headsets, rooms and management.

quiz.q: What did Yealink start with?
quiz.w: SIP phones were the early core of the company.

quiz.q: A reseller asks if Yealink really is number 1 in IP phones. Best answer?
o: Yes, it is an official fact
Yealink states this itself, based on unit shipments
quiz.w: The claim comes from Yealink's own site, so attribute it to them.

pages.t: VoIP sends voice as data packets over an IP network such as the internet, so no old phone network is needed. Think of a call travelling the same way an email does, in small pieces that are put back together.
g: Voice over IP: phone calls carried over a data network

pages.t: SIP is the common language phones use to register, dial, hold and transfer calls. An IP phone is a real desk phone that plugs into the network. A softphone is an app on a PC or mobile that does the same job.
g: Session Initiation Protocol: the common standard for setting up and ending VoIP calls
A calling app on a computer or phone

pages.t: The phone system, called a PBX, can run in the customer's own office, which is on-premises, or in a provider's data centre, which is cloud or hosted. UC then adds video meetings and messaging on top of plain calls.
g: The system that connects and routes a company's calls

quiz.q: What is a softphone?
o: A calling app on a computer or phone
quiz.w: A softphone is software that replaces the physical phone.

quiz.q: What does SIP do?
o: It sets up and controls VoIP calls
quiz.w: SIP handles registering, dialling and call control.

quiz.q: A customer has no phone system in the building and uses a provider's service over the internet. This is:
quiz.w: When the provider runs the system in its data centre, it is hosted or cloud.

pages.h: The ladder from T3 to T8
pages.t: Yealink sorts desk phones into series. T3 is entry-level and cost-effective, T4 is mid-range office phones, T5 is the prime business range, and T7 and T8 aim at managers, executives and professionals.
g: A family of phones with the same look and feature level

pages.t: The T54W is described as a mid-level phone for professionals and managers. It has Bluetooth and Wi-Fi built in, takes expansion modules for more line keys, and can link to a few DECT handsets through a dongle.
g: An add-on key panel that gives a phone more speed-dial and line buttons

pages.t: The T5 range also includes the VP59, called a flagship smart video phone. Yealink also lists a Wi-Fi phone, a 4G phone and conference phones for meeting tables, such as the CP965 for medium to large rooms.

quiz.q: Which series is Yealink's entry-level line?
quiz.w: T3 is listed as entry-level and cost-effective.

quiz.q: A busy executive wants a premium desk phone. Which end of the range?
quiz.w: T7 and T8 are aimed at executives and professionals.

quiz.q: What does an expansion module add?
quiz.w: It adds extra buttons for lines and shortcuts.

pages.t: DECT is a cordless phone standard that began in Europe. It is used mainly for voice, with fast hand-over between base stations, and is generally not disturbed by Wi-Fi. Staff can walk around the building and keep talking.
g: Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications, the standard for business cordless phones
The unit the handsets connect to

pages.t: W70B is an IP base station for small and medium businesses. For larger sites there are multi-cell systems called W90, W80 and W75 Mini MC, which join many base stations into one coverage area.
g: Several base stations working as one network so calls roam across a large area

pages.t: Handsets run from basic (W71H, W73H) to premium (W74H, W78H). Ruggedized models, such as the W57R handset and the W77P and W79P phone systems, suit tougher places like workshops.

quiz.q: Why choose DECT over a Wi-Fi phone for walking staff?
o: It is voice-focused and roams between base stations
quiz.w: DECT is built for voice and moves calls between base stations smoothly.

quiz.q: A large site needs coverage over a big area. Which fits?
o: A multi-cell system such as W80
quiz.w: Multi-cell systems combine base stations for wide coverage.

quiz.q: Which handset type is for rough environments?
quiz.w: Ruggedized handsets are built for tougher use.

pages.t: Headsets differ by link. Wired USB plugs straight into a PC, Bluetooth pairs with phones and laptops, and DECT gives wireless roaming from a base. The WH62 and WH67 are DECT models, the BH71 is Bluetooth.
g: Short-range wireless between a headset and a device

pages.t: WH62 is an entry-level DECT headset. WH67 is a convertible DECT headset with a touch-screen base that can also act as a desktop workstation. BH71 suits people on the move. UH38 is a premium USB headset with dual noise-cancelling microphones.

The CP900 was a premium portable USB and Bluetooth speakerphone for huddle rooms and on-the-go use. It reached end of sale on 22 December 2025. Always check that a model is still sold before you quote it.
g: The date a product can no longer be ordered from the vendor

quiz.q: Which Yealink headset is a premium USB model?
quiz.w: The UH38 is described as a premium USB headset.

quiz.q: A sales rep travels by train and wants one headset for phone and laptop. Which fits best?
quiz.w: The BH71 is aimed at on-the-go users who also work in the office.

quiz.q: What should you check before quoting the CP900?
o: Whether it is still on sale
quiz.w: It reached end of sale, so confirm availability first.

pages.t: A video bar puts camera, microphones and speaker in one unit. Yealink's MeetingBar range runs from the A10 (focus rooms, 1 to 4 people) and A25 to the A40 and A50, which reaches medium to large rooms.
g: One device with camera, mic and speaker built in

pages.t: The MVC series is a kit: a mini-PC, a camera system, audio gear and a touch panel. The MVC640 targets medium rooms. The MVC960 is for extra-large rooms and uses a dual 4K camera system.
g: Yealink's Microsoft Teams Rooms kits that run on Windows

pages.t: Small room: a bar. Medium room: a stronger bar or an MVC kit. Large or extra-large: MVC with extra microphones and cameras. Yealink's size ranges are rough guides, so ask about layout, ceiling and acoustics too.

quiz.q: Which device suits a small focus room for 1 to 4 people?
quiz.w: Yealink places the A10 in focus rooms and huddle spaces.

quiz.q: What is in an MVC kit?
o: Mini-PC, camera, audio gear and touch panel
quiz.w: MVC kits bundle the computer and room hardware.

quiz.q: A customer has an extra-large boardroom. Which fits?
quiz.w: The MVC960 is designed for extra-large rooms.

pages.t: Microsoft tests devices and gives passing ones the label Certified for Microsoft Teams. The tests cover audio and video quality, management and security. A device without the label has not passed that testing.
g: Tested and approved by the platform owner, here Microsoft

pages.t: Teams Rooms on Windows (Yealink MVC) suits medium to large rooms and allows more peripherals. Teams Rooms on Android (MeetingBar, DeskVision A24) is a simpler appliance for small to medium rooms.
g: A ready-made device with fixed parts, simple to roll out

pages.t: Many Yealink desk phones are open SIP devices that work with many phone systems. Teams or Zoom rooms use devices built for that platform. Yealink also lists Zoom Rooms models, including the A40 bar and the MeetingBoard.

quiz.q: What does "Certified for Microsoft Teams" mean?
quiz.w: Microsoft's program tests quality, reliability and compatibility.

quiz.q: A small room wants a simple appliance with easy rollout on Teams. Which fits?
quiz.w: The Android model is the standardised, simple option.

quiz.q: What is the risk of mixing non-certified devices in a Teams room?
o: Missing features such as remote management
quiz.w: Non-certified devices may lack auto-recognition and remote management.

pages.h: Two ways to run the phone system
pages.t: On-premise runs on a server the customer owns: more control, but hardware and IT staff are needed. Cloud-hosted runs at a provider: quick to start and updates are included, but it is a subscription with less customisation.

Yealink says its IP phones work with more than 60 IP-PBX providers, including Asterisk, 3CX and Starface for on-premise. For hosted setups it names platforms like BroadSoft and Metaswitch, and Genband.

Ask which platform the customer runs or wants, then check Yealink's compatibility information for that exact platform and phone model. Compatibility lists are dated, so confirm against current firmware before you promise anything.
g: The built-in software of a device, updated over time

quiz.q: Which describes a cloud-hosted phone system?
o: Runs on the customer's own server
quiz.w: Cloud-hosted means the provider runs it.

quiz.q: Roughly how many IP-PBX providers does Yealink say its phones work with?
quiz.w: Yealink states more than 60 providers.

quiz.q: A customer runs 3CX. What is the best first step?
o: Check the compatibility info for that phone model
quiz.w: Always verify the exact model against the platform.

pages.t: Yealink lists three: YMCS, its cloud service; YDMP, its on-premise platform; and USB Connect for USB devices. They help a reseller keep many devices updated and monitored.

YMCS lets admins deploy, upgrade, monitor and troubleshoot devices from one cloud portal. It sends alarms by email, supports bulk firmware upgrades and scheduled tasks, and is built on Microsoft Azure.
RPS is a free Yealink service. After a phone is unpacked and powered on, it is redirected to its assigned server for configuration. That saves a technician from visiting each desk.
g: Redirection and Provisioning Service: sends a new phone to its settings server automatically

quiz.q: Which platform is Yealink's cloud management service?
quiz.w: YMCS is the cloud service.

quiz.q: What does RPS save?
quiz.w: RPS redirects a new phone to its server automatically.

quiz.q: A customer has 200 phones across offices and wants bulk updates. What do you point to?
quiz.w: Bulk firmware upgrades are what management platforms are for.

pages.t: A small office on a hosted phone service: T3 or T4 phones plus simple headsets. A reception desk handling many calls: a mid-range phone like the T54W with expansion modules and a wireless headset.
Hybrid teams need a USB headset such as the UH38 at home and in the office, and a MeetingBar in small rooms. Add an MVC kit for bigger rooms on Teams. Match the platform first, the room size second.

Staff who walk around need DECT: a W70B for a small site, a multi-cell system for large ones, and a ruggedized handset where it is rough. Call centres usually start from comfortable headsets, so ask what the agents wear all day.

quiz.q: A small office needs basic desk phones. Which series first?
quiz.w: T3 is entry-level and cost-effective.

quiz.q: A warehouse team walks around all day. Which fits?
quiz.w: Cordless rugged DECT suits walking staff.

quiz.q: A hybrid firm on Teams wants a small meeting room set up. Which fits?
quiz.w: A video bar is the simple all-in-one choice for small rooms.

pages.t: Always ask first: Teams, Zoom, 3CX or another platform? The answer decides whether you quote open SIP phones or Teams or Zoom devices. A wrong platform guess can be an expensive mistake, so ask before you quote.
Microsoft requires a Teams Rooms licence (Pro or Basic) for each room device, separate from the hardware. Also check lifecycle: the MP54 Teams phone was discontinued on 30 September 2024.
g: The right to use software, often paid per device or user

pages.h: Objection: it is just a phone
pages.t: If a customer says cheaper phones exist, widen the picture: one vendor for phones, headsets, rooms and management. Ask where their time goes today: setup, support calls, or meeting rooms that fail.

quiz.q: What must each Teams room device have, apart from hardware?
quiz.w: Microsoft requires a Teams Rooms licence per room device.

quiz.q: What is the first question to ask a new customer?
quiz.w: The platform decides which devices fit.

quiz.q: A customer wants an MP54 Teams phone. What do you do?
o: Check status first, since it is discontinued
quiz.w: Discontinued products need checking and often an alternative.

pages.t: Microsoft publishes lists of certified devices, covering Teams Rooms, phones, panels and personal devices. Certification is not something only Yealink can offer, so check the current list for each model instead of assuming.

Yealink's pitch is breadth: phones, DECT, headsets, room systems and management from one maker, with Teams and Zoom devices alongside open SIP phones. Its management cloud also links to tools like Microsoft Entra ID.
Do not claim a feature you have not verified, and do not run down rivals. Say what Yealink offers, point to the datasheet and check how it fits the customer's platform, room and needs.

quiz.q: Which statement about certification is right?
o: Microsoft keeps certified lists for many device types
quiz.w: Microsoft's certified lists cover several device categories.

quiz.q: What is Yealink's main argument for a reseller?
quiz.w: One maker covering phones, headsets, rooms and management.

quiz.q: A customer asks about a feature you are unsure of. What do you do?
quiz.w: Never claim what you have not verified.
